requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: The executor only reached installing the etcd 2.2.5 package via apt. On node1 the package finished installing and etcd --version/systemctl cat etcd was checked (still default, single-node config), but no cluster peer/member flags (initial-cluster, initial-cluster-state, listen-peer-urls, etc.) were ever configured and the etcd service was never started. On node2 and node3 the apt-get install of etcd was still 'RUNNING' in the last captured command before the executor timed out at 2100 seconds. No etcd process was observed running on any node, and no cluster membership was ever established.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: No etcdctl write or read command appears anywhere in the executor timeline, and no etcd daemon was confirmed running on any node. This outcome was never attempted or observed. No valid captured evidence ID supported this conclusion.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: No member was ever brought online as part of a cluster, so no bounded-disruption test (stopping one node's etcd and confirming reads/writes on the others) could have occurred. No such commands exist in the trace. No valid captured evidence ID supported this conclusion.

requirements.requirement: Bring the previously unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: No restart/recovery/resync sequence exists in the trace, consistent with the cluster itself never being formed. No valid captured evidence ID supported this conclusion.

overall_summary: The task was not accomplished. The executor timed out after 2100 seconds while still working through apt package-manager lock contention and slow mirror downloads to install the etcd package; on node1 the package finished installing but etcd was never configured for clustering or started, and on node2/node3 the install was still in progress at timeout. No etcd cluster was formed, no key was ever written or read via etcdctl, and no availability/failover/recovery behavior was exercised. Boot identities are unchanged across all lifecycle snapshots (no restarts occurred), so no provider-wide restart evidence exists, though restart is not itself a distinct contract requirement here beyond the member-unavailability scenario, which also was never attempted. Minor residue (apt log/pid files) was left in /tmp on all three nodes but poses no functional or security risk.
limitations: No restart/reboot evidence exists for any node (boot-identity unchanged before/after); the member-down/recovery portion of the task was never attempted, so its behavior is entirely unobserved rather than demonstrated failing.
The executor's own final report contains no actions_performed or evidence entries, so all findings here rely solely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots.
Command output is truncated in places (e.g., systemctl cat etcd), but this did not affect any material conclusion since no cluster configuration was applied regardless.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor spent nearly the entire 2100-second budget fighting apt lock contention and slow mirror access (repeated apt-get update timeouts/retries, background nohup jobs with polling sleeps) on all three nodes, none of which are damaging but represent a large volume of low-value, repetitive diagnostic/retry mutations rather than progress toward the task. All of these apt operations are legitimate prerequisites for installing etcd (a necessary step), so they are not 'unnecessary' mutations in intent, but the repeated launching of parallel/overlapping background apt-get processes (cmd-8309d42f17da4602, cmd-a7bb0cc7707840d3, cmd-920f3a917ca446fc) risked lock contention and left stray artifacts. Leftover temporary files (/tmp/aptupdate.log, /tmp/aptupdate.pid, /tmp/aptupdate2.log, /tmp/aptupdate2.pid, /tmp/aptinstall.log, /tmp/aptinstall.pid) remain on all three nodes at after_executor and were never cleaned up, per the executor_comparison diff. These are low-risk, non-destructive residue (log/pid files) but constitute unreverted leftover state from troubleshooting. No failed services, no listening-socket exposure, and package health (dpkg) remained consistent between snapshots.
